forecasts.reason: Eight directions are the finishing dial, so subtracting them at 1.0 runs it backwards (on hard328 cap hits went 77 -> 96, about x1.25). Losing the top boxing direction also removes some answer endings, so the cued base's roughly 22-27 MATH-500 cap hits should rise to the high 30s.

The eight directions together act as the finishing dial. Think-SFT has about 90 cap hits but is right on 88 % of the answers it finishes, so at 1.5x (which on the base matches full RL) it should finish more, about like Think-SFT + 1x the full delta (220), up from 209.

Turning the eight-direction dial to 3x overshoots it: on the base, 3x decayed into word strings (117 vs 190 at 2x). That damage should carry over to the Think-SFT host only partly, hence a low value with a wide interval.
Only the RL directions act as the finishing dial. A random rank-8 edit was flat at every size on the base, so Think-SFT should stay at its single-sample mean of 209.

The finishing dial adds up across both rewards' eight directions. Math at 1.5x (about 200) plus Code's finishing dose pushes past the optimum, like the 2x cell (190), and Code's top direction writes code form rather than boxes.
Math top-8 at 1x (192) plus Code top-8 at 1x (Code alone 178) adds finishing dose to a total of about 1.5x Math, near the dial's optimum of about 200, with a small cost from Code's own answer form.
Random directions carry no finishing signal, so the control should score like Math's eight directions alone (about 200 at 1.5x).
Code's eight directions are the finishing dial on code (399 at 1.5x, 394 at 2x). Adding Math's eight adds more finishing past the optimum, so slightly below 399.
Code's eight at 1x (386) plus Math's eight (which alone add +6.9 over random on code) adds finishing dose toward Code's 1.5x level (399).
Random directions do nothing, so the control should score like Math's eight directions alone on code (368 of 538).

At 2x the eight-direction dial has removed nearly all cap hits (5 on hard328) while precision drops (190 vs 203 on hard328). MATH-500 has few cap hits left to convert, so the edit should land a little under the 1.5x score of 456.
